title: gh_claim.py had no requirement-label filter, could route from-scratch requirements through the wrong workflow (WF-03)
discovered_in: User question during post-hoc review of the requirement-batch loop mode built earlier this session ("Do simple loop treat the issue list in the same way, or it filter list by some label?")
symptom: tools/gh_claim.py (the GitHub-issue loop, triggered by 'start loop') queried gh issue list --state open with no label filtering -- every open issue, requirement-labeled or not, was one undifferentiated pool sorted newest-number-first. Once the requirement-batch loop (WF-02, docs/requirements.yaml) was built for the 166 label:requirement issues, this became a live routing hazard: issue #331 (BRW-SEC-1) was the single highest-numbered open issue in the whole repository. The very next 'start loop' run would have claimed it and routed it through WF-03 (Issue Resolving) -- confirmed live via a dry-run gh_claim.py invocation before this fix, which returned #528 (an ordinary bug) only because #331-#325 etc. had not yet been excluded at the time of that specific test run's data snapshot, but tracing gh_claim.py's own sort order confirmed #331 was next in line on any run made before this fix.
root_cause: Two loops were built to answer two different questions (bugs via WF-03, requirements via WF-02) but shared one undifferentiated data source (all open GitHub issues) with no label-based boundary drawn between them at the point the second loop was added.
impact: A from-scratch, never-implemented requirement issue claimed via the wrong loop would be diagnosed by ISSUE-FIXER as if the expected behaviour already existed in a requirements spec (WF-03's premise), when in fact the requirement itself needed CODE-DESIGNER + BACKEND-DEV work from scratch (WF-02's premise) -- producing either a confused/incorrect ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis or, if caught, a redundant loop back to the requirement-batch loop after wasted WF-03 steps.
evidence: Live dry-run of gh_claim.py before the fix confirmed BRW-SEC-1 (#331) was the highest-numbered open issue and would sort first. Post-fix dry-run confirmed 245 open issues -> 79 claimable by the GitHub-issue loop with zero label:requirement issues among them, highest claimable now #550 (a genuine bug).
fix_target: Added a label:requirement exclusion filter to gh_claim.py._fetch_open_issues(). Updated its module docstring and docs/agents/protocols/LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's Purpose section (previously stated the loop drains 'all open GitHub issues... requirements gaps, and anything else' -- now factually corrected to state the exclusion and why).
related_issues: ISS-0607/GH-542, ISS-0609/GH-548, ISS-0610/GH-550 -- the same loop-mode hardening session this was discovered during
The requirement-batch loop mode itself (no single ISS/GH number -- delivered across PR #552 and #553) is the counterpart this filter defers to
resolution: gh_claim.py._fetch_open_issues() now filters out any issue whose labels include 'requirement' before sorting/returning candidates. Verified via direct import test: 245 open issues reduce to 79 claimable, 0 requirement-labeled issues remain, highest-numbered claimable issue changed from #331 (BRW-SEC-1) to #550 (a genuine bug). Full gh_claim.py dry-run confirmed it correctly skips already-resolved issues (#550) and claims a real bug (#528) without ever surfacing a requirement issue; test claim discarded (local-only, never pushed) before commit.
